body:
maya: quick heads-up — running the FP8/INT8/GPTQ/AWQ bakeoff on cuda19 base image with Triton 23.11 + trtllm shim. hitting two failure modes on L40s: intermittent OOMs during long sequences and accuracy deltas (~2.4% drop) for AWQ compared to same quant build on H100. repro script attached below.

alex: can you paste the exact error log / stack? also which driver version on the L40s nodes?

maya: driver is 535.86.05, container uses libc++ / gcc 12. error snippet:

```
trtllm_plugin.so: undefined symbol: _ZN6nvinfer6plugin12createPluginEv
E TrtTritonShim: failed to load plugin, falling back to generic kernels
[W] KernelFallback: slow kernel path invoked, cuBLAS_gemm fallback triggered x12
[ERR] Allocator: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (requested 2147483648)
```

Also a bunch of linker warnings at container start: `glibc: version 'GLIBC_2.34' not found` — odd because image was built against 2.35.

sophia: that symbol lookup smells like plugin vs tensorrt ABI mismatch — trtllm plugin binary probably compiled against a different TensorRT/API surface. We saw similar when switching minor driver versions before. Are you using the vendor-provided trtlib or building from source?

maya: using prebuilt trtllm plugin from our buildcache (release-23.11). The same plugin + image worked on our H100 pool, but fails on L40s in EU region.

liam: could be subtle: L40s nodes have a slightly different libc/tls/driver stack because of the vendor kernel+dpkg. Also L40s CUDA driver reported as 535.x but firmware differs. Two quick repros: run same container with `--cap-add SYS_PTRACE` and `LD_DEBUG=bindings` to catch symbol resolution; and also try preload of system nvinfer plugin so the trtllm plugin binds to the system symbols: `LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvinfer_plugin.so.8`

toni: also check Triton server logs. If Triton loads a different libnvinfer at runtime (we have multiple versions in /opt/triton/lib), plugin load can succeed but then symbol version mismatch triggers when the plugin calls into the runtime at inference. That would explain why H100 works (different lib path order).

maya: good notes. repro command for the failing run:

```
docker run --gpus all --rm -e TRITONSERVER_LOG_VERBOSE=1 \
  -v /models/ceres-quant:/models myregistry/redwood-triton:cuda19-23.11 \
  tritonserver --model-repository=/models --strict-model-config=false
```
When the workload switches to long sequences (~2048) we see repeated slow kernel pathways and then the OOM. Shorter sequences (512) generally pass but accuracy gap persists on AWQ quantization.

alex: for the accuracy delta, are you running identical quantization artifacts (same AWQ bitwidth/scaling) on both H100 and L40s? sometimes calibration RNG or memcpy alignment causes quant stats to differ.

maya: yes same artifacts (we ship the quant files with sha256). We did notice ephemeral nondeterminism in quant eval: a few eval batches show token shift errors in the logits for AWQ-only runs on L40s.

liam: propose we split investigation: (1) plugin/driver ABI — reproduce minimal binder with LD_DEBUG and `readelf -s trtllm_plugin.so` to see symbol versions; (2) memory behavior — run with `TRTLLM_CACHE_MAX_TOKENS=1024` and `TRT_ALLOW_FP8=0` to see if FP8 path is the culprit; (3) accuracy — re-run AWQ calibration with deterministic seed + single-threaded batch to remove async effects.

toni: also try swapping to vLLM driver for the same quant artifacts. vLLM uses a different kernel path for GEMMs; if vLLM reproduces accuracy drop then it's likely quant/packing issue rather than plugin linking. If only trtllm shows the problem, it's Triton/TensorRT plugin area.

maya: ran quick tests: vLLM path did not OOM but latency was 2.2x higher; accuracy drop still ~1.9% (smaller than Triton path). So looks like both runtime and kernel choices affect numeric results.

alex: weird — different runtimes producing different numerics on same quant weights is expected to some degree, but 2% is large. Can you run a single-batch forward on both runtimes and diff logits to localize layer(s) with largest divergence? e.g., dump layer outputs for layer 12/24 and compare max abs diff.

maya: started that. quick log: layer 8 shows max abs diff ~3.1e-2 after softmax; earlier layers <1e-4. The divergence spikes after rotary+kv-caching apply.

liam: rotary implementation differences are notorious. TRTextras sometimes fuses rotary differently which could change rounding. Also FP8 quantization scaling per-head can interact with rotary. Check the pack/unpack alignment in the transformer kernel.

toni: ops for next steps: maya will gather LD_DEBUG output + `readelf` symbol versions, liam will run calibration with forced deterministic RNG, alex will schedule a small H100 vs L40s head-to-head with driver 536.40 (known-good) vs 535.86.05, and i'll open infra ticket to test an image that preloads system tensorrt plugin and forces container lib path ordering.

deploy-bot: [CI] infra/test-bakeoff-cuda19 started for pool l40s-eu (job id: 789012).

maya: thanks — will drop the reproducer/link and logs into the ticket. tagging @ops on the driver variance. :thumbsup:

(END OF THREAD)
